fieldMarks: Soft, see-through skin; pale pink to white with dark markings on the back and tail (NDOW).
Large lidless eyes with vertical pupils and sticky toe pads (NDOW).
Bumpy skin covered with small raised tubercles, which separates it from the native western banded gecko (NDOW).
behavior: Nocturnal; often seen on buildings, window screens and walls near lights hunting moths, crickets, cockroaches and spiders, hiding in cracks and crevices or under bark by day (NDOW; NatureServe).
Can vocalize with chirps and clicks and can drop its tail (NDOW).
Females lay two eggs per clutch, several clutches a year, often in communal nests (NDOW); in Texas eggs are laid May to early September (NatureServe).
habitat: In North America usually on or in occupied buildings, on walls and ceilings; also under palm leaves, in bark crevices and rocky outcrops (NatureServe; NDOW).
range: Introduced in North America. Native to the Mediterranean region and nearby (NatureServe; NDOW); established from Florida to Texas and north into southeastern states, in Arizona and southern California, and in southern Nevada urban areas (NatureServe; NDOW).

lookalikes.name: Western banded gecko
lookalikes.howToTell: Native western banded gecko lacks the Mediterranean gecko's raised tubercles on bumpy skin (NDOW).
